Chromatic

Privacy policy

Last updated September 18, 2026

Chromatic is a macOS color contrast checker made by Andrew Gioia. This policy describes how the app handles information.

No tracking or data collection

Chromatic does not collect or transmit personal information, track your activity, or include advertising or third-party analytics. No account is required. Color processing and contrast calculations take place on your Mac.

Information stored on your Mac

Chromatic saves your preferences and a history of up to 10 recently picked colors locally on your Mac. These values are used to remember your settings and let you reuse colors. They are not sent to Andrew Gioia or to a server operated for Chromatic.

Color history remains until you clear it or newer choices replace older entries. You can remove it at any time by choosing “Clear history” in the history menu. Preferences remain locally until changed or the app’s stored settings are removed. Copies may also exist in backups you manage through macOS or other software.

Screen color picking and the clipboard

Chromatic uses the macOS color picker and screen color sampler when you choose to pick a color. It uses the selected color value; the app does not record your screen or save screenshots of its contents.

When you choose a copy command, Chromatic writes the requested color value or contrast results to the system clipboard. It does not monitor or read your clipboard. Clipboard content is handled by macOS and any clipboard tools you use.

Apple services

Apple handles App Store downloads, purchases, and any system diagnostics you choose to share under its own settings and privacy policy. Chromatic does not include its own analytics or crash-reporting service.

Changes to this policy

If Chromatic’s privacy practices change, this page will be updated with a new date.

Contact

For information about the developer and ways to get in touch, visit andrewgioia.com.
